rationales: Genus is a taxonomic rank above species.
Order is a higher taxonomic rank than species.
Species is the basic unit of classification.
Class is a higher taxonomic rank than species.
Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane.
Active transport moves molecules against a concentration gradient, from lower to higher concentration.
Passive transport moves substances down their concentration gradient.
Diffusion is movement from higher to lower concentration.
Metabolic activity is not at its highest during prophase.
Metaphase is a stage of chromosome alignment during cell division.
Interphase is when the cell grows and carries out intensive metabolic activities.
Anaphase is a stage of chromosome separation during cell division.
Lipase does not digest starch; amylase does.
Lipase does not digest proteins; proteases do.
Vitamins are not substrates for lipase.
Lipase catalyzes the breakdown of lipids.
A habitat is the place where an organism lives, not the group itself.
The biosphere includes all regions of Earth where life exists.
A community consists of populations of different species living together.
A population is members of the same species living in the same place at the same time.
Physiology is the study of how organisms and their parts function.
Morphology is the study of form and structure.
Histology is the microscopic study of tissues.
Ecology studies relationships between organisms and their environment.
Plasmodium is the microorganism that causes malaria.
Entamoeba causes amoebic dysentery, not malaria.
Paramecium is a free-living protozoan and does not cause malaria.
E. coli is a bacterium and is not the cause of malaria.
Related genera are grouped together in a family.
A phylum is a much higher taxonomic rank than genus.
A class is a higher taxonomic rank than genus.
An order contains related families, not genera directly.
Peroxisomes carry out oxidation reactions, not protein synthesis.
Lysosomes digest cellular materials.
Vacuoles mainly store substances and help maintain cell pressure.
Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis.
Plastids perform functions such as photosynthesis and storage, but are not the cell's main energy-producing centres.
Mitochondria produce most of the cell's usable energy through cellular respiration.
Ribosomes synthesize proteins.
Golgi bodies modify and package substances.
Sea stars can regenerate lost parts through cell division, including mitosis.
Horses do not regenerate lost body parts in this way.
Mosquitoes do not regenerate lost body parts in this way.
Frogs do not regenerate lost parts as effectively as sea stars.
Formic acid is not a vitamin coenzyme.
Nucleic acid is not a vitamin.
An amino acid is a protein building block, not a vitamin coenzyme.
Folic acid is a vitamin that functions in coenzyme forms in metabolism.
Stomata cover about 1–2% of the leaf surface.
A coverage of 1–5% is not the stated approximate value.
A coverage of 5–10% is too high.
A coverage of 2–8% is too high.
Zinc is a micronutrient but is not the answer for nitrogen metabolism here.
Iron has roles in enzymes and electron transport but is not the specified nutrient here.
Chlorine is important in photosynthesis and osmosis, not the specified nitrogen-metabolism role.
Nickel is required for nitrogen metabolism, including the activity of urease.
Protein provides about 4 kilocalories per gram, not 8.
Protein provides more than 2 kilocalories per gram.
One gram of protein provides about 4 kilocalories of energy.
Protein provides more than 2 kilocalories per gram.
